content: I'll read the test image to analyze the plant disease symptoms.

**Analysis of the test image:**

**Affected plant part:** Stem — specifically at a node/junction area, shown close-up being held by a hand.

**Key visual features:**
1. **White cottony mycelium** covering the stem surface, particularly dense at the node
2. **Small black sclerotia** (hard fungal resting bodies) scattered within and on the white mycelial mass
3. **Bleached/straw-colored dead stem tissue** visible on the right side — classic "timber rot" appearance where stem tissue turns white and papery
4. The stem appears constricted/collapsed at the infected node
5. White residue also coating the dead right-stem section

**Reasoning through the differential:**

- **Southern Blight** (*Sclerotium rolfsii*): Produces white fan-like mycelium with small round tan-to-brown sclerotia, typically at the soil line — possible, but sclerotia here appear black and the location is not clearly at soil line.
- **Sclerotinia Timber Rot** (*Sclerotinia sclerotiorum*): Produces white cottony mycelium externally, hard black sclerotia (internally and on surface), and bleached/whitened dead stem tissue (hence "timber rot"). The combination of white mycelium + black sclerotia + bleached dead stem stubs is the diagnostic hallmark of this disease.
- Other diseases (bacterial, viral, leaf-targeting) don't fit the stem presentation with sclerotia.

The bleached, straw-colored dead stem to the right combined with white cottony mycelium and visible black sclerotia is the textbook presentation of **Sclerotinia Timber Rot**.
